newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president signs 1997 privatisation plan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president signs 1997 privatisation plan.

text.p: Ukraine President Leonid Kuchma has approved plans to sell off thousands of companies this year in a much-delayed privatisation programme, the presidential press service said on Wednesday.
Kuchma signed a decree to privatise 1,440 medium and large companies and about 3,400 small enterprises in 1997, it said.
The main sales will be in agriculture and food processing, where 780 medium and large companies will be sold, says the programme obtained by Reuters.
Other companies to go under the hammer will be in the transport, machine-building, military, oil and gas sectors.
Ukraine has nearly finished selling off small businesses and is proceeding with medium and large-scale privatisation, including enterprises deemed strategic to national security.
But to date it can name only Ukrainsky Richkovy Flot (Ukrrichflot), the country's largest shipping company, as a large-scale privatisation success story.

The State Property Fund, the main privatisation agency, says that around 9,000 medium and large businesses are currently undergoing privatisation. Since January 1995 more than 70 of the shares of 5,000 medium and large companies have been sold.
Foreign buyers are to pay for purchases of shares in Ukrainian companies with compensation certificates or in hryvnias from accounts in Ukrainian banks.
Compensation certificates were issued to Ukrainians whose savings were gobbled up by inflation when Ukraine won independence in 1991.
